lines.japanese: その後、俺は風見が丘まで徒歩で戻ってきた。
lines.english: Afterward, I walked all the way back to Kazamigaoka.

lines.japanese: 国内有数の繁華街、その沈まない人工の太陽に背を向け、一時間強の道のりを速足で進んだ。
lines.english: I turned my back on one of the country's busiest nightlife districts and its artificial sun that never sank, covering the hour-plus journey at a hard pace.

lines.japanese: 帰る道すがら、短時間でなにを言うべきか、考えをまとめておきたかったからだ。それは徐々に固まっていった。
lines.english: I needed the walk home to put my thoughts in order—to decide what I had to say in the little time left. Bit by bit, I found the words.

lines.japanese: 周辺のどこの家もがそうであるように、未明の羽田邸は生活の音と光一切を落とし、夜と同一化していた。
lines.english: Like every house around it, the Haneda home before dawn lay dark and silent, absorbed into the night.

lines.japanese: 俺は小鳩を起こさないよう、静かに鍵を挿す。
lines.english: Careful not to wake Kobato, I eased the key into the lock.

lines.japanese: 「ただいま」
lines.english: “I’m home.”

lines.japanese: そして、帰りを待つ者のいない闇の中へ滑りこんだ。
lines.english: Then I slipped into the darkness where nobody waited for my return.

lines.japanese: 靴を脱いでまっすぐ二階へ向かおうとしたが、踏み段を三つ四つ上がったところでふと思いなおして立ちどまった。
lines.english: Shoes off, I headed straight upstairs. Three or four steps up, I reconsidered and stopped.

lines.japanese: 「んー……飲んどくか」
lines.english: “Hmm... Might as well have one.”

lines.japanese: 俺は階段を引きかえし、音が立たないよう注意しながら廊下を渡ってダイニングへ入った。
lines.english: I went back down, crossed the hall as quietly as I could, and entered the dining room.

lines.japanese: 暗がりに慣れてきた目と、明るみで見た記憶を頼りに、戸棚の小さなガラス戸を開ける。タカシの叔父貴が仕事疲れの風呂上がりや週末のナイター観戦時に嗜む、洋の東西もろもろな丸ビン角ビンが並んでいた。
lines.english: With eyes adjusting to the dark and memory of the room in daylight, I opened the cupboard's little glass door. Round bottles, square bottles, from East and West—the collection Takashi's uncle enjoyed after a bath at the end of a hard day's work or while watching weekend night baseball.

lines.japanese: 俺はひとつずつビンの口に触れてすでに開栓済みのものを探し、その中から適当な一本の首を掴んで抜きだした。
lines.english: I ran my fingers over each bottle top until I found one whose seal had already been broken. Then I caught it by the neck and pulled it free.

lines.japanese: 暗さでラベルは判然としなかった。しかし肉厚の角張ったガラスの手触りが、ロックグラスの中で涼やかに氷を鳴らす蜂蜜色の液体を想起させた。
lines.english: The dark concealed its label. But the feel of that thick, angular glass called up honey-colored liquor, ice chiming coolly in a rocks glass.

lines.japanese: 俺は栓を開けて直接ボトルに口を付けた。甘くてきつい香りが鼻に染みた。目を閉じてゆっくり傾けると、生ぬるい苦味が舌を通り、その奥へ流れおちていった。
lines.english: I opened the bottle and put it straight to my lips. A sweet, harsh smell stung my nose. Eyes closed, I tipped it slowly; lukewarm bitterness crossed my tongue and ran down my throat.

lines.japanese: 「──っぷぁ」
lines.english: “—Pah.”

lines.japanese: 数回喉を鳴らしたあとでボトルを戻した。液体の通り道が焼きつくように熱かった。俺は咳きこみそうになるのをなんとか堪えていた。
lines.english: After several swallows, I put the bottle back. The liquor had seared a line all the way down my throat. I just managed not to cough.

lines.japanese: 戸棚を閉めてから台所で蛇口をひねり、首を傾けてカルキ臭いチェイサーをがぶがぶ飲んだ。
lines.english: I closed the cupboard, turned on the kitchen tap, tilted my head beneath it, and gulped a chlorine-scented chaser.

lines.japanese: 「まじぃ……」
lines.english: “Disgusting...”

lines.japanese: 手の甲で口元を拭ってから、排水口へ唾をひとつ吐いた。
lines.english: I wiped my mouth with the back of my hand and spat once down the drain.

lines.japanese: トイレで小用を済ませてから二階へ上がった。
lines.english: After taking a leak, I went upstairs.

lines.japanese: タカシの部屋と小鳩の部屋を通りすぎて、突きあたりの扉へ向かう。
lines.english: I passed Takashi's room, passed Kobato's, and headed for the door at the end.

lines.japanese: ようやく喉の痛みが引いて、早くも頬が火照ってきた。
lines.english: At last my throat stopped hurting. Already, heat was rising into my cheeks.

lines.japanese: 真夜中の静寂の中で、板張りの廊下がぎしりと鳴いた。
lines.english: In the midnight stillness, the wooden hall gave one creaking cry.

lines.japanese: 部屋に入るとフローリングの床にスポーツバッグを置きすて、照明もエアコンも点けずに机へ向かった。
lines.english: Inside my room, I dropped the sports bag on the hardwood floor and went to the desk without turning on the lights or the heat.

lines.japanese: 天板の上から紙とペンを掴む。そのまま後ろ向きに一歩さがり、カーテンも閉めないままベッドへ仰向けに倒れた。
lines.english: I grabbed a sheet of paper and a pen from the desktop. Then, without even drawing the curtains, I took one step back and let myself fall backward onto the bed.

lines.japanese: 手の中のものを頭の横へ放ると、俺は冷えた布団の上で暗い天井を見つめながら、襟元を楽にしてジーンズのベルトを緩めた。
lines.english: I tossed the things beside my head and stared at the dark ceiling from atop the cold bedding, loosening my collar and the belt of my jeans.

lines.japanese: 「ふぅぅぅ……」
lines.english: “Haaaaah...”

lines.japanese: 長く長く息を吐いて、そっと目を閉じた。
lines.english: I breathed out for a long, long time and gently closed my eyes.

lines.japanese: ここからがめんどくさい。
lines.english: Now for the hard part.

lines.japanese: 千歳鷲介がかつて明晰夢の原理を応用して編みだした≪面談≫という交流手段は、それまでの単なる筆談に革新的な確実性をもたらした。
lines.english: The communication method Shusuke Chitose had devised using the principles of lucid dreaming—the *Interview*—had brought a startling new certainty to what had once been no more than an exchange of notes.

lines.japanese: しかし、何度試してもなかなか慣れないものだ。
lines.english: No matter how many times I tried it, though, I never quite got used to it.

lines.japanese: 俺は鳴みたいに口を半開きにし、努めて頭の中を空っぽに保った。
lines.english: I let my mouth hang half open like Naru and worked to keep my mind empty.

lines.japanese: 何も……何も考えず……。
lines.english: Nothing... Think of nothing...

lines.japanese: ただ凍えた沈黙にたゆたい……眠りと酩酊の訪れに身を委ねよう……。
lines.english: Drift in frozen silence... surrender to sleep and drunkenness as they come...

lines.japanese: そうして俺は、浅い霞が思考を白く覆うに任せた。
lines.english: I let a pale mist spread white over my thoughts.

lines.japanese: ……ねむい。
lines.english: ...Sleepy.

lines.japanese: ふと気付いたら……眠かった。
lines.english: The next thing I knew... I was sleepy.

lines.japanese: 気だるい眠気とゆるやかな浮遊感にまどろむ。
lines.english: I drifted in a languid drowsiness, buoyed by a gentle sensation of floating.

lines.japanese: 我に返れば、数瞬前の自分が夢うつつのどちら側にいたのかも分からない──そんな眠りのほとりに俺はいた。
lines.english: Whenever awareness returned, I no longer knew which side of waking and dream I'd occupied a moment before. I had reached the shore of sleep.

lines.japanese: 部屋の空気はひどく冷えこんでいるのに、体はどこか妙に温まっている。
lines.english: The air in the room was bitterly cold, yet my body had grown strangely warm.

lines.japanese: いい頃合だ。始めよう。
lines.english: This was the right moment. Time to begin.

lines.japanese: 俺はぼんやりと、努めてぼんやりと“思考”せずに“意識”する。
lines.english: Dimly—as dimly as I could—I kept myself aware without letting myself *think*.

lines.japanese: 頭が冴えないよう、この中途半端な覚醒の状態を保つよう“意識”する。
lines.english: I held in my awareness the need to stay half-awake, careful not to let my head clear.

lines.japanese: ゆっくりと、慎重に……しかし慎重であることさえ考えないよう漠然と……曖昧に、抽象的に、感覚的に、内なる自分を体から剥がしてゆく──
lines.english: Slowly, carefully... yet vaguely enough not even to think of care... indistinctly, abstractly, by sensation, I peeled the self within away from the body—

lines.japanese: ──剥がしてゆくさまを、イメージする。
lines.english: —I pictured it peeling free.

lines.japanese: 横たわった体の内側が、すべて濃白色の揺らめく気体でもうもうと満たされているイメージ。
lines.english: The body lying there: hollow, filled end to end with dense white vapor, seething and astir.

lines.japanese: 内なる洞で逆巻く濃白色の気体を、四肢の先端からひとところ、頭頂部へと集積させるイメージ。
lines.english: I pictured the dense white vapor churning through that inner hollow, gathering from the tips of all four limbs into one place: the crown of my head.

lines.japanese: 頭頂部に集積した成田隼人の≪精髄≫を、頭の内側でゆっくり旋回させるイメージ。
lines.english: I pictured the *essence* of Hayato Narita, amassed at my crown, revolving slowly inside my head.

lines.japanese: ゆっくり旋回させながら、白く霞んだ尾を引きながら、明滅を繰りかえしながら、濃白色の≪精髄≫が螺旋の軌道を徐々に細めてゆくイメージ。
lines.english: Turning slowly, trailing white mist, blinking in and out, the dense white *essence* tightened its spiral little by little.

lines.japanese: ゆっくり旋回しながら、螺旋の中心を目指し、底の見えない空洞を深く深く潜ってゆくイメージ。
lines.english: Still revolving toward the spiral's center, sinking deep, deeper into a hollow without visible bottom.

lines.japanese: 深く、深く、深く……。
lines.english: Deeper. Deeper. Deeper...

lines.japanese: よし──鐘よ、鳴れ。
lines.english: All right—let the bell ring.

lines.japanese: そう祈ると、教会の荘厳な鐘の音が鳴りひびく。召集の鐘の音だ。
lines.english: At my prayer, a solemn church bell pealed: a bell calling us together.

lines.japanese: ずん……と二本の足に重みがのしかかり、天地の感覚を取りもどし、肉体の感覚を取りもどし、俺は想念の世界でまぶたを開ける。
lines.english: Weight settled—heavy—onto two feet. Earth and sky returned. Body returned. In the world of thought, I opened my eyes.

lines.japanese: 礼拝堂に立っていた。
lines.english: I stood inside a chapel.

lines.japanese: 広すぎる堂だった。広くて静かで、そして尊い。しかし気が遠くなるほどの高みにある天井は、逆に閉塞感を覚えさせる。
lines.english: It was far too vast. Vast and still and holy. Yet the ceiling soared so high it made my head swim, and somehow that made the place feel more confining.

lines.japanese: 窓から射しこむ目映い光を手で遮って、俺は指の隙間から中央の祭壇に目を凝らした。そこは常に何者かの存在を感じさせながら、常に何者の姿も存在しなかった。
lines.english: Shielding my eyes from the dazzling light pouring through the windows, I peered between my fingers toward the central altar. I always sensed someone there, though no one ever appeared.

lines.japanese: 俺は身じろぎするように祭壇へ一歩だけ近付いた。おんぼろスニーカーが毛足の浅い絨毯を踏むと、その繊細な音すら静寂の堂内に染みわたった。
lines.english: I edged one step toward the altar. My battered sneaker pressed the low-pile carpet, and even that delicate sound soaked through the silent nave.

lines.japanese: 落ちつかない気分で歩を止め、俺は舌先で内側から頬を膨らませた。
lines.english: Uneasy, I stopped and pushed my cheek outward from within with my tongue.

lines.japanese: 鳴りやまぬ鐘の音に急かされて、背後の扉がひとつ開いた。俺はそちらへ振りむいた。
lines.english: As though hurried by the ceaseless bell, one of the doors behind me opened. I turned toward it.

lines.japanese: そこには五つの扉が連なっているが、開くのはいつもひとつだけだった──右から二番目の待機室。
lines.english: Five doors stood in a row, but only one ever opened: the *Waiting Room* door second from the right.

lines.japanese: 「ぐっもー」
lines.english: “Mornin'.”

lines.japanese: 出てきたのは、もちろん千歳鷲介だ。
lines.english: Naturally, Shusuke Chitose emerged.

lines.japanese: 「隼人くんから≪面談≫のお誘いなんて久しぶりだわあ。いったい何事かしら」
lines.english: “It’s been ages since you invited me to an *Interview*, Hayato. Whatever could this be about?”

lines.japanese: やつは伸びをしながら絨毯の上を進み、あくびでもするみたいに言った。
lines.english: He stretched as he crossed the carpet and spoke as if the sentence itself were a yawn.

lines.japanese: 「へらへらしてんじゃねえよ。ブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Quit grinning or I'll fucking kill you, asshole.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、はは……まあ、だいたい想像は付くけどさ」
lines.english: “Ah—haha... Well, I can more or less guess.”

lines.japanese: 鷲介は下唇を突きだして溜息を吹きあげた。前髪が揺れる。そのまま引っくりかえりそうになるほど首を仰けぞらせて、はるか頭上を見やった。
lines.english: Shusuke pushed out his lower lip and blew a sigh upward, stirring his bangs. Then he bent his neck so far back he looked ready to topple and stared into the heights.

lines.japanese: 「ねー、いま≪コックピット≫は？」
lines.english: “Hey—who's in the *Cockpit* right now?”

lines.japanese: 「無人に決まってんだろ」
lines.english: “Nobody, obviously.”

lines.japanese: 「まー、そりゃそうか」
lines.english: “Well, yeah. Guess so.”

lines.japanese: 鷲介は頭の位置そのまままに、皮肉めいた瞳だけ真横へ流した。固く閉ざされた待機室のドア群をちらりと一瞥、そしてまた真上を眺める。
lines.english: With his head still thrown back, Shusuke slid a sardonic glance sideways at the tightly sealed row of *Waiting Room* doors, then looked straight overhead again.

lines.japanese: 「ボディはどこに置いてあんの？」
lines.english: “Where'd you park the body?”

lines.japanese: 「羽田の家……つか、おまえのベッドの上」
lines.english: “At the Haneda house... On your bed, actually.”

lines.japanese: 「ふうーん」
lines.english: “Hmmm.”

lines.japanese: やつは一転、首を思いっきり真下へ曲げて片手でとんとん叩き、長椅子の一端に腰を下ろした。
lines.english: In one abrupt reversal, he bent his neck as far downward as it would go, gave it a few pats with one hand, and sat at the end of a pew.

lines.japanese: 「ま、時間も限られてることだし？　さっそくご用件を伺いましょうか？」
lines.english: “Well, time is limited, isn't it? Shall we get straight to business?”

lines.japanese: 「おまえ、鳳翔って知ってる」
lines.english: “You know Kakeru Otori?”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 俺がその名前を口にすると、さも意外といったように鷲介はぽかんとだらしない顔をした。
lines.english: At the name, Shusuke's face went slack with what looked like honest surprise.

lines.japanese: 「カケルくんが、なに？」
lines.english: “What about Kakeru?”

lines.japanese: 「……やっぱ知ってんだ」
lines.english: “...So you do know him.”

lines.japanese: 思ったとおりだ。あいつが言った「おまえたち」というのは、そういう意味か。
lines.english: Just as I'd thought. So that was what 'all of you' meant.

lines.japanese: 「なあ。おまえの知ってる鳳ってどんなやつ」
lines.english: “Tell me. What’s he like—the Otori you know?”

lines.japanese: 「どんなって……ええと、新進気鋭のイラストレーター？」
lines.english: “What is he like...? Let's see. A brilliant young illustrator on the rise?”

lines.japanese: 「直接の面識はねえの」
lines.english: “You haven’t actually met him?”

lines.japanese: 「んーん、しょっちゅう会うよ。まあ、約束して会うってより偶然ばったりって方のが多いけど」
lines.english: “I have. I see him all the time. Usually we just run into each other instead of making plans.”

lines.japanese: 「偶然ばったり」
lines.english: “Happen to bump into each other.”

lines.japanese: 俺とやつの距離に似てる。
lines.english: It sounded much like the distance between him and me.

lines.japanese: 偶然ばったり──ハ、面白い冗談だ。
lines.english: Happen to bump into each other. Hah. Some joke.

lines.japanese: 「うん、たまにバイト紹介してもらったりもするしね。今やってるアレキサンダーを教えてくれたのも元々は彼でさ──」
lines.english: “Yeah. Sometimes he finds me part-time work, too. He's actually the one who first told me about Alexander, where I'm working now—”

lines.japanese: 「やつの性格は」
lines.english: “His personality.”

lines.japanese: 俺は鷲介の長くなりそうな話に割りこんで尋ねた。やつは口を開けたまま、不思議そうに俺を見た。なぜそんなことを聞くのか、という顔だった。
lines.english: I cut into Shusuke's story just as it threatened to run long. He stared at me with his mouth still open, puzzled. His face asked why I wanted to know.
“His personality...?”

lines.japanese: 「そう。千歳鷲介が知ってる鳳翔の人となりは」
lines.english: “I mean, what kind of man is Kakeru Otori to *you*, Shusuke Chitose?”

lines.japanese: 「んー、そうねえ……なんてゆーか、ちょっとトボけたところあるけど、基本的にえらく冷めた子だよね」
lines.english: “Hmm... How do I put this? A little spacey, maybe, but basically an awfully detached kid.”

lines.japanese: 「つねに無気力、つねに無関心、つねに無愛想。だけど幼い子供みたいに、些細な皮肉や嫌味で相手の興味を引こうとしちゃう、実は寂しがりんぼさん？」
lines.english: “Always listless, always indifferent, always unfriendly. But like a little boy, he tries to catch people's attention with petty sarcasm and spite. Secretly a lonely little thing?”

lines.japanese: 俺は頭を落とし、さらに溜息を落とした。
lines.english: I dropped my head, then let another sigh fall after it.

lines.japanese: 「え、どしたの隼人くん」
lines.english: “Uh, what’s wrong, Hayato?”

lines.japanese: 「……俺の知ってる鳳翔は、血に飢えた猛禽みてーなイカれジャンキーだ」
lines.english: “...The Kakeru Otori I know is a deranged junkie, like a blood-starved bird of prey.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「柳木原フレイムバーズっていうストギャンもどきの幹部やってる」
lines.english: “He’s an officer in a wannabe street gang called the Yanagihara Flame Birds.”

lines.japanese: 鷲介のへらへらが固まり、驚きに打たれた目が丸く膨れあがった。
lines.english: Shusuke’s loose grin froze. His eyes went round with shock.

lines.japanese: 「そ、それっ！　柳木原なんちゃら団！　きのう米田さんに聞いた……ちょっ、それ……ええっ、その話ホントなの？」
lines.english: “Th-that! That Yanagihara-whatever gang! Mr. Yoneda told me yesterday... Wait, that... Huh? Is that really true?”

lines.japanese: 「本当も何も、俺に言わせりゃ鳳翔ったら、まずそれしか出てこねえよ」
lines.english: “Of course it’s true. When I hear Kakeru Otori’s name, that’s the first thing that comes to mind. Pretty much the only thing.”

lines.japanese: 「うそぉ……いや、だって彼、ちょっと可愛げはないけど、無愛想なだけの普通の男の子よ？」
lines.english: “No way... I mean, he isn't exactly lovable, but he's just an ordinary unfriendly boy, isn't he?”

lines.japanese: 普通の！　俺は思わず肩を揺らした。
lines.english: Ordinary! My shoulders jumped in spite of me.

lines.japanese: 「違う。俺の知ってる鳳翔は常軌を逸してる。敵を狩ることに悦びを見出す。芝居がかったかすれ声で話し、そのうちの半分は狂気めいた笑いが占める。ほろ酔いの躁病患者みたいなやつだ」
lines.english: “No. The Kakeru Otori I know is beyond reason. He delights in hunting enemies. He speaks in a theatrical rasp, and lunatic laughter fills half his words. Like a manic with a couple of drinks in him.”

lines.japanese: 「え……あの、それは俺の知ってるカケルくんとぜんぜん違うんですけど」
lines.english: “Um... That doesn't sound anything like the Kakeru I know.”

lines.japanese: 「みてーだな。いや、でもそんなんはこの際、些細な問題だ。重要なのは、やつは俺とおまえだけじゃなく、タカシの人格まで知ってるってコト」
lines.english: “Apparently. But right now that's minor. What matters is that he knows Takashi too—not only you and me.”

lines.japanese: 「は……え、うそ、それってかなりよろしくないんじゃないの」
lines.english: “Wha... Wait, seriously? Isn't that extremely bad?”

lines.japanese: 「そんでいちばん重要なのは、伊丹伽楼羅まで知っていたコトだ」
lines.english: “Most important: he even knew Karura Itami.”

lines.japanese: 「いたみ……って誰？」
lines.english: “Itami...? Who's that?”

lines.japanese: 「俺たちの中にいる、もうひとり。通称ガルーダ。俺に言わせりゃキング・オブ・マッドマン」
lines.english: “One more person inside us. Goes by Garuda. Far as I’m concerned, king of the madmen.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ？　え、それって、なんで俺たちの中に？　うそん、そんなの聞いたことも話したこともないよ？」
lines.english: “What? Why would someone like that be inside us? No way. I've never heard of him, much less spoken to him.”

lines.japanese: 「俺だって初耳だったっつの。だけど接触してみて分かった。あいつはヤベえ。いろいろヤベえ。けど困ったことに、やつは異常なほど≪コックピット≫に執着してる」
lines.english: “It was news to me too. But I made contact. Now I know: he's bad. Bad in every possible way. And the real trouble is his insane obsession with the *Cockpit*.”

lines.japanese: 「とどめに鳳翔と顔見知り……どころか、鳳は伊丹伽楼羅にご執心だ。これほど最悪な状況だったってのに、今まで気づきもしなかったんだから、俺たちも間抜けだよな」
lines.english: “To top it off, he knows Kakeru Otori. More than knows him—Otori is obsessed with Karura Itami. Things were this bad and we never noticed. Pretty damn stupid of us.”

lines.japanese: 「へー……そう、そうなんだ……」
lines.english: “Oh... Right. I see...”

lines.japanese: 鷲介が珍しく神妙なツラをしていた。横を向いた目はどこか遠くを眺めていた。
lines.english: For once, Shusuke looked grave. His gaze had turned aside, fixed on something far away.

lines.japanese: 俺よりもずっとおめでたい頭をしている鷲介のこと、もしかしたら身近な人間にひどく裏切られた心境にあるのかもしれない。
lines.english: Shusuke was even more blissfully clueless than I was. Maybe he felt horribly betrayed by someone close to him.

lines.japanese: 「いや、しかし参ったなあ、カケルくんがそんな厄介な子だったなんて思わなかったよ」
lines.english: “Still, this is a problem. I never dreamed Kakeru was such a troublesome kid.”

lines.japanese: 「俺またてっきり、時間延長多すぎだ、ブッ殺すぞコノヤロウなんて話だと思ってたからさ、軽くショックだよ」
lines.english: “I was sure you'd called to say I keep blowing past my time slots and I'll fucking kill you, asshole. So this is a little shocking.”

lines.japanese: 「おう、そういえばその話もしなくちゃな」
lines.english: “Oh, right. We need to talk about that too.”

lines.japanese: <8>\「藪をついたら蛇が出た！」
lines.english: “Talk about poking a hornet’s nest!”

lines.japanese: 「違げーって。おまえさ、どうなの。上手くやってんの」
lines.english: “That's not what I meant. How's it going? You managing okay?”

lines.japanese: 「は？　ああいや、上手くっていうかそれなりに？」
lines.english: “Huh? Oh. Managing... well enough, I guess?”

lines.japanese: 「あんさ、実は俺さ……今回おまえの知らないところで小鳩を危険な目に遭わせてんのよ。悪い」
lines.english: “Listen, the truth is... This time, while you weren't looking, I put Kobato in danger. Sorry.”

lines.japanese: 「はー、まあ、そんな危ない子に付きまとわれてたらねえ」
lines.english: “Well, yes. If a dangerous kid like that has been stalking you...”

lines.japanese: 何があってもおかしくないけどさ、という表情を鷲介は浮かべた。
lines.english: His face added, *With a kid like that, anything could happen.*

lines.japanese: 「だから決めた。俺は降りる」
lines.english: “That's why I've decided. I'm bowing out.”

lines.japanese: 「降りるって？　どういう意味？」
lines.english: “Stepping down? What do you mean?”

lines.japanese: 「消えるって意味」
lines.english: “I mean I'm disappearing.”

lines.japanese: 鷲介が表情を隠したのが分かった。当たり前だ、俺だってどんな顔をすればいいのか分かんねえ。
lines.english: I saw Shusuke mask his expression. Naturally. I didn’t know what face to make either.

lines.japanese: 「だから、交替時間のことは気にしなくていいから。おまえはおまえで頑張れよ」
lines.english: “So don’t worry about the handoff times. Just do what you can on your end.”

lines.japanese: 「え、隼人君って、そんな人の心配とかしてくれる子だっけ」
lines.english: “Huh. Hayato, were you always the type to worry about other people?”

lines.japanese: 「さあな。じゃ、あとは頼んだ。伊丹とかいうやつ、それと鳳には気をつけ……」
lines.english: “Who knows. Anyway, the rest is yours. Watch out for that Itami bastard—and Otori—”

lines.japanese: 「……時間切れか」
lines.english: “...Out of time?”

lines.japanese: 俺たちは揃って頭上を仰いだ。目覚めが近い。思考の霞が晴れようとしている。
lines.english: We looked up together. I was close to waking; the haze over my thoughts was beginning to clear.

lines.japanese: 鷲介は間もなく訪れる解散のときを待ちながら、天窓から射す白い光に目蓋をなかば閉じた。
lines.english: Shusuke half closed his eyes against the white light streaming through the skylight and waited for the meeting to dissolve.

lines.japanese: 「いや、実は俺さあ、世話になってる女のひとから、彼を更正させろって言われてるんだよね」
lines.english: “Well, actually, there's this woman who's helped me out, and she asked me to set him straight.”

lines.japanese: 「更正！　あの真性ジャンキーを！」
lines.english: “Set him straight? That dyed-in-the-wool junkie?”

lines.japanese: 「無理かなあ」
lines.english: “Think it’s impossible?”

lines.japanese: 「ハ！　いいじゃん、ぜひ為しとげてくれよ。それが出来たら俺はおまえに土下座──」
lines.english: “Hah! Go on, then—pull it off. If you can, I’ll even get down on my hands and knees—”

lines.japanese: 「──してもいい」
lines.english: “—if I have to.”

lines.japanese: 唇から漏れた、真実、知覚できる声に目を覚ました。
lines.english: I woke to the sound of my own voice, real and audible, escaping my lips.

lines.japanese: 鷲介のにやけ面も、荘厳な鐘の音も、まばゆい陽の射す礼拝堂も、すべてが一瞬に消えうせていた。
lines.english: Shusuke's smirk, the solemn bells, the chapel washed in brilliant sun—all vanished in one instant.

lines.japanese: 俺は六畳一間の小さな部屋で深く息を吐いた。両手の指を握ったり開いたりしてみる。
lines.english: I let out a long breath in the tiny room, barely ten square meters, and flexed the fingers of both hands.

lines.japanese: 凍えた部屋を照らすのは、遠く住宅街の薄明るい水銀灯だけだった。
lines.english: Only the pale mercury lamps of the distant neighborhood lit the frozen room.

lines.japanese: 枕元のメモとペンを手探りで拾って、俺は余熱のように残っていた眠気混じりの倦怠感を振りはらった。
lines.english: I groped for the note and pen beside my pillow and shook off the drowsy lethargy lingering like residual heat.

lines.japanese: ベッドから這いおり、鷲介の机にかぶりつき、やつと交換した情報を箇条書きで記してゆく。
lines.english: I crawled off the bed, hunched over Shusuke's desk, and listed the information we'd exchanged.

lines.japanese: ≪面談≫の中で交わした会話は、夢の中の体験と同じで、目覚めてしまったあとにはそのほとんどが記憶として永続しない。
lines.english: Words exchanged in an *Interview* were like a dream: once awake, almost none of them endured as memory.

lines.japanese: 俺はほとんど「てにをは」も省略して、ただ要点だけを覚えているうちに殴り書きした。
lines.english: I scrawled the essentials while I still remembered them, leaving out practically every little linking word.

lines.japanese: とくに『伊丹伽楼羅』という項目は三重四重のマルでくくって強調した。
lines.english: I circled the entry *Karura Itami* three or four times over for emphasis.

lines.japanese: 「よし……こんなもんか」
lines.english: “All right... That should do.”

lines.japanese: 書きとめてペンを置くころには、新しい眠気があくびを伴ってやってきた。
lines.english: By the time I finished writing and set down the pen, a fresh wave of sleepiness arrived with a yawn.

lines.japanese: 「ふぁあ……寝るか」
lines.english: “Haaah... Time for bed.”

lines.japanese: 俺は着ていたものを脱ぎちらかすと、冬の寒さに震えながら下着姿で廊下へ飛びだした。
lines.english: I stripped and left my clothes wherever they fell, then dashed into the hall in my underwear, shivering in the winter cold.

lines.japanese: それからタカシの部屋へ行き、タカシの部屋着を身につけ、タカシの布団を敷いて眠りについた。
lines.english: I went to Takashi's room, put on Takashi's loungewear, laid out his bedding, and went to sleep.

lines.japanese: 目覚まし時計は四時間後に鳴るようセットされていた。
lines.english: The alarm was set to ring four hours later.

lines.japanese: 毎朝、寝不足での通学ご苦労さまです。
lines.english: Thanks for dragging yourself to school on too little sleep every morning.

lines.japanese: おやすみなさい。
lines.english: Good night.
